subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The nature of God and the covenant
The use and authority of scripture

questions.q: The Tenakh is divided into three sections. What does the name Tenakh stand for?
questions.explain: Tenakh is an acronym for the Torah (Law), Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings).

questions.q: How many books make up the Torah?
questions.explain: The Torah consists of the five books of Moses, from Genesis to Deuteronomy.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five books of the Torah?
questions.explain: Psalms belongs to the Ketuvim (Writings), not to the five books of the Torah.

questions.q: What is the name of the central Jewish declaration of God's oneness?
questions.explain: The Shema is the declaration affirming belief in the one God of Israel.

questions.q: The Shema begins, 'Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is...' which word?
questions.explain: The Shema affirms strict monotheism by declaring that the Lord is One.

questions.q: With whom did God make the covenant sealed by circumcision (brit milah)?
questions.explain: God's covenant with Abraham was marked by the circumcision of Jewish males.

questions.q: What was the sign of God's covenant with Noah?
questions.explain: God set a rainbow in the sky as the sign of the covenant made with Noah.

questions.q: What is the handwritten scroll of the Torah used in the synagogue called?
questions.explain: The Sefer Torah is the handwritten parchment scroll read during synagogue services.

questions.q: The word 'Torah' is most often translated into English as which of the following?
questions.explain: Torah means 'teaching' or 'law', reflecting its role as instruction for living.

questions.q: The Oral Torah was eventually written down. In which text was it first recorded?
questions.explain: The Oral Torah was first set down in writing in the Mishnah.

questions.q: The Talmud is made up of the Mishnah together with which other text?
questions.explain: The Talmud combines the Mishnah with the Gemara, its commentary and discussion.

questions.q: Jews describe God as omnipotent. What does this mean?
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful, so God is believed to have unlimited power.

questions.q: Judaism is described as monotheistic. What does this mean?
questions.explain: Monotheism is the belief in a single God, central to Jewish faith.

questions.q: At Mount Sinai God made a covenant with the Israelites through Moses. What was central to this covenant?
options: The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.explain: The Sinai covenant centred on God giving Moses the Torah and Ten Commandments.

questions.q: Why is a yad (pointer) used when reading from the Sefer Torah?
options: To avoid touching the sacred parchment directly
To mark where the scroll ends
questions.explain: The yad allows the reader to follow the text without touching the holy scroll by hand.

questions.q: Where in the synagogue is the Sefer Torah kept?
questions.explain: The Sefer Torah is stored in the Ark, the most honoured place in the synagogue.

questions.q: A sofer (scribe) notices that a single letter has been written incorrectly on a new Torah scroll. What does Jewish practice show about this?
options: The whole scroll may be invalid until the error is corrected
The error does not matter because the meaning is unchanged
The scroll must be burned immediately
Only rabbis may now read from it
questions.explain: A Sefer Torah must be copied with total accuracy, so even one wrong letter can make it unfit for use.

questions.q: A Jewish father arranges for his eight-day-old son to be circumcised. Which covenant is he continuing?
questions.explain: Circumcision on the eighth day continues the covenant God made with Abraham.

questions.q: A student wants to read the accounts of creation and of the Exodus from Egypt. Which part of the Tenakh should they turn to?
questions.explain: Both creation (Genesis) and the Exodus (Exodus) are found within the Torah.

questions.q: During the festival of Simchat Torah a congregation celebrates joyfully. What are they marking?
options: The completion and restarting of the yearly Torah reading cycle
The building of the Temple in Jerusalem
The beginning of the weekly Sabbath
questions.explain: Simchat Torah celebrates finishing the annual Torah readings and immediately beginning again.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Judaism: Beliefs & Scriptures
